halfLife.notes: Half-life shorter than the clinical response window. Chrono (extended-release) formulation allows once-daily dosing in some patients. Valproate INHIBITS LTG metabolism — LTG dose must be halved when co-prescribed. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

activeMetabolite.name: Valproate-4-ene (minor)
activeMetabolite.notes: No clinically significant active metabolite for mood purposes. The hepatotoxic metabolite (4-ene-valproate) is relevant in overdose and paediatric use.

cypInteractions.switchingRelevance: Valproate is a potent UGT inhibitor — it roughly DOUBLES lamotrigine levels. When starting valproate in a patient on lamotrigine, halve the lamotrigine dose. When stopping valproate in a patient on lamotrigine, increase lamotrigine dose (levels will fall). Interaction with carbamazepine is complex: CBZ induces valproate clearance, reducing VPA levels. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

reboundPsychosisRisk.notes: No major rebound psychosis risk but abrupt discontinuation can precipitate seizures or mood relapse. Taper recommended. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

formulationNotes: Epilim Chrono (extended-release) preferred for BD dosing and smoother levels. Divalproex (Depakote) may have better GI tolerability. ALL formulations carry the same teratogenicity risk. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
specialConsiderations: TERATOGENICITY (DANGER): Highest teratogenic risk among mood stabilizers. Associated with neural tube defects, major congenital malformations (6–11%), and neurodevelopmental disorders in children exposed in utero. CONTRAINDICATED in women of childbearing potential unless all alternatives are inadequate and EURAP-equivalent risk minimisation is in place.
EURAP / MIMS Malaysia restriction: As of 2023, valproate may only be prescribed to women of reproductive age under a risk minimisation programme. Document consent and contraceptive use.
Monitoring: LFTs and full blood count at baseline and 6-monthly. Valproate levels not routinely required for mood disorders unless toxicity suspected.
Weight gain: significant — counsel from initiation. Associated with polycystic ovary syndrome in women.
Hair loss (alopecia): can occur — consider zinc/selenium supplementation.
Hepatotoxicity: rare but potentially fatal in children under 3 years on polypharmacy. Adults lower risk but check LFTs.
citations: MHRA Valproate Medicines Update (2018, applicable in Malaysian prescribing context)
